jobs.occupation: Senior Software Engineer - Portfolio Analysis
jobs.description:
**What Makes Us, Us

**Join some of the most innovative thinkers in FinTech as we lead the evolution of financial technology. If you are an innovative, curious, collaborative person who embraces challenges and wants to grow, learn and pursue outcomes with our prestigious financial clients, say Hello to SimCorp!

At its foundation, SimCorp is guided by our values — caring, customer success-driven, collaborative, curious, and courageous. Our people-centered organization focuses on skills development, relationship building, and client success. We take pride in cultivating an environment where all team members can grow, feel heard, valued, and empowered. If you like what we’re saying, keep reading!

**WHY THIS ROLE IS IMPORTANT TO US

**Portfolio Analysis is where investment professionals turn data into insight on portfolios, performance and risk. Our products are business critical and widely used, so they need to keep evolving in a responsible way. Right now that means strong maintainability, high system performance, mature CI/CD, and reshaping parts of SimCorp Dimension for the cloud.

As a Senior Software Engineer in our Product Division, you will join an agile team of 5–7 people in the Portfolio Analysis Product Area. You will mainly work on backend components, APIs and services, using C#, .NET, Dyalog APL and Oracle.

AI is part of how we work every day. We see it as a natural part of modern software engineering, alongside source control, testing, CI/CD and code reviews. AI does not replace engineering judgment. It helps good engineers learn faster, reduce repetitive work and build better software.

**What You Will Be Responsible For

**

• Understand and challenge customer requirements together with your team, then design, implement, test and support the chosen solutions

• Design, develop and maintain backend functionality and APIs using C# and .NET, and work with Dyalog APL where it is part of the product

• Contribute to cloud modernization and scalable service design where it adds real value

• Improve performance, maintainability, testability and developer experience

• Take ownership beyond code: contribute to design discussions and help the team make sound technical decisions

• Use CI/CD, automated testing and code reviews as natural parts of daily engineering work

• Use AI every day in practical engineering work, such as exploring ideas, understanding unfamiliar code, prototyping, improving tests, documenting decisions and automating routine tasks

• Help the team discover where AI creates real value and where traditional engineering judgment should lead

• Collaborate with product owners, domain experts and fellow engineers to turn customer needs into good software

**What We Value

**How you gained your skills matters less than your ability to learn, collaborate and take ownership. We expect you to know some of the following and to be interested in learning the rest:

• C# and .NET development, backend development and API design

• Building high-performance, scalable and maintainable applications

• Continuous integration and delivery, automated testing and practical quality engineering

• Relational databases, preferably Oracle or similar

• Cloud technologies, distributed systems or Azure-based services

• Willingness to learn additional technologies, including Dyalog APL

• Curiosity about AI-assisted software engineering and daily use of modern tools

• Experience with financial instruments or investment systems is an advantage but not a requirement. We will bring you up to speed through training and a comprehensive onboarding program.

We also value people who take ownership and deliver results. We look for engineers who try new approaches, work with others to leverage everyone’s strengths, and balance technical quality with business value. We want you to help build an inclusive, trust-based engineering culture.

**Benefits

**

• Global hybrid work policy – We ask you to work 2 days a week from the office. You can work remotely the other days if you choose.

• Growth and innovation – Every sixth sprint is reserved for planning, innovation, learning and improvements.

• Self-direction – Teams and developers have a high degree of freedom to plan, organize and design their work.

• Modern engineering in a real product context – You will work on cloud modernization, AI-enabled development and performance in large-scale financial software.

• Inclusive and diverse company culture – We want people to bring different perspectives and contribute to a respectful workplace.

• Work-life balance – We believe balance between professional and private life makes us better colleagues and better engineers.

• Empowerment – All voices are valuable, and you will be involved in shaping our work processes.

**NEXT STEPS

Please send us your application in English via our career site as soon as possible, we process incoming applications continually. Please note that only applications sent through our system will be processed.** At SimCorp, we recognize that bias can unintentionally occur in the recruitment process. To uphold fairness and equal opportunities for all applicants, we kindly ask you to exclude personal data such as photos, age, or any non-professional information from your application. Thank you for aiding us in our endeavor to mitigate biases in our recruitment process.

If you are interested in being a part of SimCorp but are not sure this role is suitable, submit your CV anyway. SimCorp is on a positive growth journey, and our Talent Acquisition Team is ready to assist you discover the right role for you. The approximate time to consider your CV is three weeks.

We are focused on continually improving our talent acquisition process and making everyone’s experience positive and valuable. Therefore, during the process we will ask you to provide your feedback, which is highly appreciated.

**Who We Are

**We are 3,000 colleagues with a broad range of nationalities, education, professional experience, and backgrounds. SimCorp is an independent subsidiary of Deutsche Börse Group. For over 50 years, we have worked closely with investment and asset managers to become the world’s leading provider of integrated investment management solutions. We are an equal-opportunity employer committed to building a culture where diverse perspectives and skills are integrated into our everyday work.

jobs.occupation: Data manager for Center for Landscape Research in Sustainable Agricultural Futures, Land-CRAFT, Department of Agroecology, Aarhus University
jobs.description:
Department of Agroecology at Aarhus University, Denmark, is looking for a full-time Data manager to work at the Center for Landscape Research in Sustainable Agricultural Futures (Land-CRAFT).

Land-CRAFT addresses three of our major societal challenges - food security, climate change, and loss of biodiversity. With Center partners from University of Copenhagen, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (Germany), and Colorado State University (USA), we bring together expertise in climate impact research, landscape analyses, biogeochemistry, agronomy, biology, and geography to develop solution – oriented research that extends across multiple spatial and temporal scales. Established in June 2022, Land-CRAFT has built a dynamic team to undertake both fundamental and applied research aimed to reduce the environmental impact of agricultural systems, specifically regarding greenhouse gas emissions. To reach our goals, we are using a combination of empirical, field-based approaches, digital technologies, including modelling and remote sensing, while closely interacting with stakeholders. The position we advertise here is aimed at supporting these activities with respect to data management. The new employee will become part of a support team with complementary skills and work collaboratively in an active and international research environment with diverse projects and people across Department of Agroecology.

The position is available from 1st March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The duration of the position is 3 years.

Responsibilities and tasks
Your main role as part of the support team at Land-CRAFT will be to support research activities of the staff and research students (at BSc, MSc, and PhD levels) in data management, analysis and statistics. This will include maintaining and supplementing relational databases used for process-based modelling and geospatial data analyses. Main responsibilities and tasks include:

• 
Organize, archive, and document data collected by the Land-CRAFT team, including with appropriate metadata protocols

• 
Manage data transfer/sharing among Center partners and external collaborators following FAIR data principles, AU rules and regulations, and GDPR rules

• 
Manage user access and permissions within the AU File system and user data on a computational server

• 
Create and manage a database on research outputs from the Center, including e.g., publications, citations and other reports, to facilitate website updates, annual reports, and other communication platforms, as well as managing the Zenodo community

• 
Support staff and students with statistical and geospatial analyses (e.g. in R and Python)

• 
Support/manage data collection pipeline from instruments in the lab & field (including visualisation of data in e.g. Origin)

• 
Establish, maintain, and refine documentation regarding all data-related protocols (e.g. data policy, data management plans, etc.)

• 
Coordinating data management across the Department of Agroecology (about 20 % of time) in collaboration with the department’s data steward

Your profile
As a member of the Land-Craft support team, we expect you to plan and perform your tasks independently and initiate frequent feedback and communication with Land CRAFT researchers and students. The position requires that you can communicate with and support students and scientists from BSc to Professor levels, including attention to detail and quality (QA/QC) and an affinity for knowledge-sharing, e.g., in working with students as they learn to manage their own data. You have a high proficiency in English, are culturally sensitive, and can work in a large group of diverse colleagues and students. At Land-CRAFT we emphasize good relationships among colleagues and students. It is therefore important that you have a positive and open personality, stay engaged with emerging challenges and opportunities, and are ready to support colleagues when needed.

Qualifications

• 
MSc in data science, agroecology, geoscience, biology, ecology, environmental science, mathematics, geography (or related fields)

• 
Knowledge and understanding of data management plans, metadata systems, archiving practices

• 
Experience in statistical analysis; knowledge of R or Python, as well as visualisation platforms

• 
Good collaboration and communications skills across different groups of employees,

• 
High level of English proficiency and cultural sensitivity

• 
Interest in and willingness to acquire general knowledge about Land-CRAFT’s research areas

• 
Familiarity with the Danish administrative structures or Danish language.

Workplace
The place of work is Aarhus University, Ole Worms Alle 3, DK-8000 Aarhus C. The affiliation will be with the Department of Agroecology.

Who we are
At the Department of Agroecology, our main goal is to contribute to sustainable solutions to some of the world’s biggest problems within the areas of soil, plants, animals, humans, and the environment. We want to make a difference by contributing to both fundamental knowledge generation and the attainment of sustainable production systems via innovative research, contracted policy advice, and education. We offer professional laboratories, greenhouses, semi-field, and field-scale research facilities, advanced computing capacities as well as an extensive national and international researcher network. The department consists of nine research sections with around 350 highly skilled employees, of which approximately 50% are scientific staff. More information can be found here.
We believe in encouraging inclusion, acceptance, and understanding by employing staff who bring unique perspectives to our department.

What we offer

• 
A collaborative, international research environment that combines high academic standards with an informal and supportive atmosphere. We value accountability, curiosity, flexibility, and teamwork in everything we do.

• 
An inclusive and respectful workplace culture, where mutual trust, kindness, and professional dialogue are part of daily life. We encourage open communication and develop a cohesive sense of community across teams and disciplines.

• 
A flexible working environment that supports work-life balance and individual needs.

• 
An active institutional commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion – in recruitment, career development, and everyday interactions.

• 
An innovative and meaningful workplace where your work contributes to solving real-world challenges. No two days are alike, and we welcome creative thinking and new ideas.

• 
Support for international researchers and their families, including Relocation Service and an Expat Partner Programme

Contact information
More information can be obtained from Klaus Butterbach-Bahl (klaus.butterbach bahl@agro.au.dk).

Formalities and salary range
Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions..You will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

About Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment for its 37,500 students, including PhD students, and has 9,000 employees (full-time equivalents) and an annual revenue of EUR 1.2 billion. Learn more at international.au.dk

jobs.occupation: Team Lead - Software Development
jobs.description:
Stay close to the code. Lead a development team. Help shape how we build software at Dalux.

Dalux is growing, and we are looking for experienced software developers who want to combine hands-on engineering with technical leadership.

As a Team Lead, you lead from within the development team. Around half of your time is spent developing software, while the rest is focused on technical direction, product collaboration, planning, mentoring, and helping your team perform at its best.

You will have significant influence on both the products we build and how we build them – including how we use agentic AI across software development.

Your role

Each Dalux development team owns one or more areas of our product portfolio, including its functionality, architecture, quality, performance, reliability, and long-term technical health.

As Team Lead, you are the technical anchor of the team. You work closely with developers, a Product Manager, and a Product Designer to understand problems, set technical direction, and turn product priorities into high-quality software.

This is primarily a technical leadership role rather than a traditional people-management position, and you will spend approximately 50% of your time developing software hands-on.

The rest of your role typically includes:

• Setting technical direction and defining architectural solutions with the team

• Working with the Product Manager to understand requirements, challenge scope, and translate priorities into development work

• Planning and prioritizing work while maintaining a healthy and sustainable flow

• Helping the team break down complex technical and product problems

• Mentoring developers through technical sparring, reviews, and day-to-day collaboration

• Taking responsibility for the quality and long-term health of your team's software

• Identifying opportunities to improve architecture, tools, development practices, and ways of working

• Driving improvements beyond your own team when they can make Dalux Development better

We expect Team Leads to have opinions, challenge existing approaches, and create clarity when there is no obvious answer.

Leading development with agentic AI

We are significantly increasing our use of agentic AI in software development.

We use and explore AI across the development lifecycle – from understanding problems and navigating codebases to implementation, testing, debugging, refactoring, and review.

As a Team Lead, you are expected to have hands-on experience using agentic AI in your own development workflow. The specific tools matter less than how you use them: providing the right context and direction, critically evaluating the output, and knowing when to intervene or take a different approach.

Your role goes beyond your own workflow. You will help your team experiment with agentic development, identify where it genuinely improves engineering effectiveness, share useful practices, and maintain the engineering judgment and quality standards required for production software.

AI can increase what capable developers can achieve, but responsibility for architecture, correctness, maintainability, and quality remains with the team.

Technologies we work with

Our platform is built on a distributed cloud architecture using AWS.

Depending on the team, you may work with technologies such as:

• Full-stack: C# / .NET, Angular / TypeScript, GitHub Copilot, MSSQL, Elasticsearch, WebGL, DirectX

• Mobile: .NET MAUI, Vulkan

• AI and Computer Vision: C++, Python, computer vision and machine learning technologies

Which team you lead depends on your technical background, interests, leadership experience, and where we see the strongest match.

Product development at Dalux

Our developers do more than implement specifications.

Developers, Product Managers, and Product Designers work together to understand problems and find solutions that balance user value, usability, technical feasibility, business viability, and long-term technical health.

As Team Lead, you bring the technical perspective into those discussions. You help the team understand why we are building something, challenge proposed solutions when necessary, and ensure technical considerations are part of product decisions from the beginning.

Your background

You are an experienced software developer who enjoys taking responsibility beyond your own code.

You may already be a Team Lead or Lead Developer. Or you may be the developer others turn to when a difficult technical decision needs to be made, a problem needs structure, or another developer needs help moving forward.

We expect that you:

• Have solid professional software development experience

• Have at least six months of practical experience using agentic AI as part of your software development workflow

• Have an educational background in Software Engineering, Computer Science, or a closely related technical field

• Have experience taking a key technical role within a development team

• Are comfortable making and facilitating technical decisions

• Enjoy mentoring and helping other developers improve

• Can create structure and direction without controlling every detail

• Have strong communication, facilitation, and planning skills

• Care about maintainability, reliability, performance, and engineering quality

• Understand how to balance short-term delivery with long-term technical health

• Can identify opportunities to improve development practices and ways of working

Experience with our exact technology stack is useful, but technical judgment, leadership ability, and strong software engineering fundamentals matter more.

What You Can Expect From Dalux

Dalux is a software company at heart, and software development is central to how we create value.

As a Team Lead, you can expect:

• Hands-on engineering – leadership does not mean leaving software development behind

• Real technical influence – short paths between ideas, discussions, and decisions

• Meaningful team ownership – teams own both product functionality and the technology behind it

• Strong technical colleagues – daily sparring with developers who care about what they build

• Close product collaboration – developers work directly with Product Managers and Product Designers

• Room to improve how we work – Team Leads are expected to challenge and evolve our development practices

• An environment actively investing in agentic AI – with the opportunity to shape how your team works with it

• High levels of trust and freedom in how you and your team solve problems

All Dalux software development takes place in-house at our headquarters in Vibenshuset, Copenhagen.

We believe working together in person makes technical collaboration, mentoring, knowledge sharing, and fast decision-making significantly easier.

About Dalux

Dalux is a Danish software company founded in 2005 by Bent Dalgaard and Torben Dalgaard.

We build digital tools that make the construction industry smarter and more efficient. Using our own 3D BIM technology, we develop software used in more than 140 countries worldwide.

Our core technology is developed entirely in-house, giving our developers and technical leaders the opportunity to influence both the products and the technology behind them.

Ready to lead from within the team?

If you want greater technical responsibility and influence while continuing to build software hands-on, we would like to hear from you.

If agentic AI is already part of how you develop software, tell us how you use it – and how you think a development team can use it effectively without compromising engineering quality.

We recruit continuously and hire multiple Team Leads as Dalux continues to grow.

If you have questions about the position, contact IT Talent Acquisition Specialist Line Hassenkam Klinge on LHP@dalux.com

jobs.occupation: Sr Lead Corporate Investigator
jobs.description:
**Your impact begins here

**As Sr Lead Corporate Investigator in Global Investigations, you will design and lead internal investigations into alleged misconduct, including fraud, bribery and corruption, conflicts of interest, potential misconduct in external engagements, and misappropriation of company assets or information. You will turn evidence into clear findings and practical recommendations, working across Novo’s global organisation as a trusted partner with the highest standards of integrity. You will create impact by safeguarding Novo and protect the trust of patients and society, to ensure Novo can pursue its purpose of driving change for lasting health.

**What You’ll Bring

**

• A Master’s degree in Business Administration, Accounting, Audit, Law, Finance or equivalent. A Bachelor’s degree combined with extensive relevant investigative experience (for example in law enforcement) also qualifies.

• Experience conducting investigations, including interviews, evidence review, root-cause analysis, reporting and remediation recommendations.

• Experience in compliance, internal investigations, legal, audit or similar in a global organisation, and in building trusting relationships across hierarchies and cultures.

• Experience leading sensitive investigations with discretion, independence and professionalism.

• Strong analytical skills and the ability to translate complex information and data into practical insights and recommendations.

• High ethical standards, sound judgement and the ability to build trust and rapport with all parties during an investigation.

• Excellent communication skills, with stakeholders across a global organisation and at all leadership levels.

• A curious and independent mindset, a proactive approach and the ability to work closely with a team of experienced professionals.

**Useful, But Not Essential

**

• Experience in compliance, internal investigations, legal or audit in the pharmaceutical industry.

• Experience in data analytics, data visualisation, AI/ML, automation and continuous improvement.

• A Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE) or similar certification.

**What You’ll Do

**You will own investigations from the first allegation to the conclusion and recommendation and support the continuous development of the Global Investigations function.

• Review and assess allegations, scope actionable investigation plans and identify key witnesses, documents and systems for evidence collection.

• Collect and review data and documentation, conduct witness and subject interviews, and develop clear, well-documented findings and recommendations.

• Keep case documentation and investigation reports timely, complete and in line with department standards.

• Identify systemic issues and root causes, and recommend corrective and preventive actions where applicable.

• Provide oversight, guidance and informal leadership to junior investigators, as well as regional and local investigators.

• Contribute to the continuous improvement of Global Investigations, including its procedures, tools and processes, to ensure alignment with industry best practice.

**Who You’ll Work With

**You will be part of Global Investigations within Business Assurance & Compliance, where colleagues safeguard the business and ensure Novo can deliver on its purpose. You will work as a peer with fellow investigators in a trusting and supportive team.

Your close partners include the wider Legal & Compliance organisation (LECX) both at headquarters and across all EVP areas, including regional and local levels, as well as a range of other key stakeholders, including HR, Global Security and Global IT Security. You will also work with external legal counsel and external investigation support when cases require it.

The role has global reach. You will work with colleagues at every level, including senior leadership, bringing clarity and professionalism to investigations across Novo. Occasional travel should be expected, sometimes at short notice.

**What You Can Expect Here

**You will have real ownership. We trust you to work independently, make tactical decisions and use your judgement within our standard investigation framework.

You will be part of a department that seeks to continuously improve itself, and where your experience and insight can bring real change. You will grow through the complexity of the work and through collaboration with colleagues across Novo, in a culture where honest feedback and high standards go together with respect and support.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 651,000.00 to 956,900.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

**Start now

**Your impact begins today. If you are ready to lead investigations and bring impact across Novo, apply for the Sr Lead Corporate Investigator role by 24 November 2026. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

For further information, please contact Mads Pazyj at ymdp@novonordisk.com

jobs.occupation: Principal Software Engineer
jobs.description:
The Siteimprove Search Insights team builds the tools our customers use to understand and improve how their content performs in search, both in classic search engines and in the AI assistants that increasingly answer questions on their behalf. We work at enterprise scale, with large volumes of crawled and third party search data, visibility and ranking analysis, and features that turn that data into recommendations marketers can act on.

We are also changing how we build. AI is part of every step, from requirements, to breaking work down, to implementing and reviewing it with coding agents. We are looking for a Principal Software Engineer who wants to build this way, and who helps us define the standard while we do it.

Tech stack you will be working with

• C# and .NET, TypeScript, React

• AWS, Terraform, Docker, Kubernetes

• Event driven services and large scale data pipelines

• GitHub Actions for CI and CD

• Claude Code and other coding agents, MCP servers, Jira and Confluence as the working surface for the AI PDLC

What we will be doing

• Contribute to the technical direction of the team. Write the system designs for the work you own, take part in design reviews, and argue for the option you believe is right.

• Design and build systems yourself: services, APIs and data pipelines that stay stable, fast and affordable as data volumes grow.

• Lead our use of AI across the product development lifecycle. Take a product requirements document to a technical vision and system designs, break it into epics and user stories that an agent can act on, and set the standard at each step.

• Improve the scaffolding that makes agent driven delivery work: context and instruction files, prompts and skills, and the review and testing practice that keeps quality high when code arrives faster than before.

• Keep search data trustworthy, with tests, monitoring and errors a colleague can understand.

• Define how we measure quality, detect drift, and explain results to customers who make decisions based on them.

• Mentor engineers at all levels through design reviews, pairing and written technical proposals, including how to work well with agents.

• Treat cost, performance and operability as design inputs from the start.

• Take part in the daily work of the team: refinement, estimation, prototyping, debugging and production support.

• Travel may be required; a valid passport is required

• Perform other duties as assigned

What we will require of you

jobs.occupation: 4 PhD positions in AI-accelerated development of PFAS-free polymer-based battery materials cells in Self-driving Laboratories - DTU Energy and BRIGHT
jobs.description:
Are you interested in a career in AI for materials and in accelerating the green transition? If so, we have a number of positions at DTU that might just right for you. 

The four PhD positions at DTU Energy are part of BRIGHT's mission-oriented Novel Biomanufacturing-Enabled Materials research programme, referred to as Mission 1A, which aims to create new classes of PFAS-free functional biomaterials through biotechnology. The mission's current focus are proteinaceous materials with defined composition, programmable chemistry and controlled assembly as sustainable alternatives to persistent fluorinated materials. The scientific scope spans AI-guided protein and peptide design, microbial engineering, non-canonical amino acid biosynthesis and incorporation, cell-free prototyping, fermentation, purification, materials processing, analytical quality control and structure-function characterization. The programme focuses on building an integrated pipeline from molecular design to scalable biomanufacturing and material testing, with explicit attention to manufacturability, cost, sustainability and industrial translation. Batteries provide the first proof-of-concept application, because PFAS-containing materials are currently used in several battery components and because this sector imposes strict requirements for stability, processability and performance. The broader ambition is to establish a versatile biomanufacturing platform for advanced PFAS-free materials with future relevance across energy technologies, coatings, electronics and other high-value applications.

You will work closely with experimental and computational colleagues in BRIGHT and in DTU Energy, as well as with our international collaborators, e.g., on the use cases on advanced battery materials in MaterialsCommons for Europe and on the development of Self-driving Laboratories (SDLs) at the Pioneer Center CAPeX. 

Responsibilities and qualifications
All four positions are centered on the application of novel PFAS-free proteins and polypeptides for applications in sustainable batteries. The design space for finding optimal compositions and synthesis conditions for such polymers for use as, e.g., electrolytes, binders and additives is vast, we are combining self-driving labs, high-throughput machine learning simulations, and agentic AI to transition to digitalization-based autonomous development of high-performing PFAS-free polymer materials for high-performant batteries, i.e., high electrochemical stability, ionic conductivity, coulombic efficiency, and cyclability at a low cost. The positions will target for areas specifically

• Development of automated setup for high-throughput testing of solid polymer electrolytes and binders, e.g., chemical and electrochemical stability, preparation and film casting. 
• Development of automated setup for in situ polymerization of sodium/sodium-based based battery materials
• Self-driving lab modules for autonomous testing of mechanical properties of polymer-based battery materials, interfaces and layers
• Self-driving lab modules for assembly and testing of advanced (e.g., solid-state and anode-less, sodium-based button and coin cell batteries.
Qualifications:

• Good working knowledge of electrochemistry.
• Ability to work independently and plan and carry out complicated tasks.
• Good communication skills in English, both written and spoken.
• A proactive approach to problem-solving, capable of identifying new directions and opportunities within the project.
Desirable Qualifications:

• Experience with self-driving laboratories or building custom experimental hardware

Application procedure

About BRIGHT – The Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition
The Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition (BRIGHT) is a major initiative based at DTU that aims to accelerate the development of biosolutions and strengthen the bio-based economy. BRIGHT serves as a hub for academic and industrial partners working together to unlock the potential of bioproduction. BRIGHT focuses on three main areas: Sustainable materials (Developing bio-based alternatives to fossil-derived materials), Microbial foods (Innovating food production through microbial technologies), and Microorganisms for net-zero agriculture (Creating solutions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in agriculture). The goal is to develop and scale innovative biosolutions within these areas, ultimately creating sustainable and competitive alternatives to fossil-based products and processes that can make significant contributions to reducing global greenhouse gas emissions.

The Department of Energy Conversion and Storage (DTU Energy) focuses on research and development of functional materials, components, and systems for sustainable energy technologies. jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in Experimental Quantum Nanophotonics
jobs.description:
PhD Project in quantum and nonlinear light–matter interactions in plasmonic nanocavities

  The Niels Bohr Institute
 Faculty of SCIENCE

  University of Copenhagen

  The Niels Bohr Institute invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in experimental quantum nanophotonics. The project will be part of the newly established Mikkelsen Photonics group (Quantum, nonlinear and nanoscale light–matter interactions), funded by a Novo Nordisk Foundation RECRUIT grant.

  Start date is (expected to be) 15 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The project

  Plasmonic nanocavities confine light to volumes thousands of times below the diffraction limit. In such extreme gaps, emission rates are enhanced by orders of magnitude, strong field gradients appear, and the usual rules of light–matter interaction are rewritten. The project builds on a wafer-scale platform developed in the group, in which colloidal quantum emitters (quantum dots or nanoplatelets) are deterministically placed into thousands of lithographically defined nanocavities with a controlled number of emitters per cavity. The PhD student will develop this platform and use it to study one or more of the following:

   	
• Few-emitter quantum optics: single-photon emission, collective emission, energy transfer and strong coupling with one to a few emitters per cavity. 	
• Cavity-enhanced nonlinear optics: using the extreme field confinement and field gradients of the nanogap to enhance and control nonlinear processes. 	
• Active and electrically tunable nanocavities: integrating functional materials (e.g. ferroelectric or two-dimensional materials) into the gap to switch and tune the emitter–cavity interaction.   The work is primarily experimental and involves nanofabrication, optical spectroscopy (photoluminescence, single-photon and photon-correlation measurements, nonlinear spectroscopy), optoelectronic device characterization and electromagnetic simulations. The specific project will be defined together with the successful candidate.

  Who are we looking for?

  We are looking for candidates within the fields of electrical engineering, physics, nanoscience, photonics, materials science or related areas. Applicants can have a background from optoelectronic or nanophotonic devices, semiconductor nanomaterials, optical spectroscopy, nanofabrication or electromagnetic simulation, but we will also consider candidates with different backgrounds. Hands-on experience with optical experiments and an interest in building new experimental setups is an advantage.

  Our group and research – and what do we offer?

  The Mikkelsen Photonics group was established at the Niels Bohr Institute in 2026, when Prof. Maiken H. Mikkelsen moved from Duke University (USA) supported by a Novo Nordisk Foundation RECRUIT grant. The group studies quantum, nonlinear and nanoscale light–matter interactions in plasmonic nanocavities and is building a new laboratory combining deeply subwavelength cavities, single-photon spectroscopy, femtosecond pump–probe spectroscopy and, in a later phase, cryogenic and high-magnetic-field operation. As one of the first members of the group, the PhD student will have a central role in shaping the experiments and the scientific direction, with close supervision. The group is part of the Quantum Optics and Photonics research area at the Niels Bohr Institute, home to the Center for Hybrid Quantum Networks (Hy-Q), and has access to the nanofabrication facilities at the Niels Bohr Institute and the DTU Nanolab cleanroom.

  The group is a part of the Niels Bohr Institute, Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. We are located in Copenhagen, in the new laboratory and office building of the Niels Bohr Institute.

  We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories and new, dedicated optics and nanofabrication facilities.

  Principal supervisor is Prof. Maiken H. Mikkelsen, The Niels Bohr Institute, maiken.mikkelsen@nbi.ku.dk.

  The PhD programme

  Depending on your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as either:

  Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Option B: An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelor’s degree.

  ************************************************************************

  Option A: Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. Electrical Engineering, Physics, Nanoscience, Photonics or Materials Science. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment in the regular programme
 Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor’s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of the integrated programme
 To be eligible for the integrated scholarship, you are (or are eligible to be) enrolled at one of the faculty’s master programmes in Physics.

  Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

  The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years, and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see: www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

  Until the MSc degree is obtained, (when exactly two years of the full 3+5 programme remains), the grant will be paid partly in the form of 48 state education grant portions (in Danish: “SU-klip”) plus salary for work (teaching, supervision etc.) totalling a workload of 150 working hours per year.

  A PhD grant portion is currently (2026) DKK 7.426 before tax.

  When you have obtained the MSc degree, you will transfer to the salary-earning part of the scholarship for a period of two years. At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Responsibilities and tasks in both PhD programmes

   	
• Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme (ONLY when you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme) 	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE

• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project   We are looking for the following qualifications:

• Good language skills   ************************************************************************

• Original diplomas for Bachelor or Master and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Publication list (if possible) 	
• Reference letters (if available)   When you will be affiliated with the University of Copenhagen or otherwise have access to their research, you may be required to undergo a background screening. The purpose is to protect the security and research integrity of the University of Copenhagen.

  Application deadline:

  The deadline for applications is 26 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process
 After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

  The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified and, if so, for which of the two models. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held shortly after the application deadline.

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact the principal supervisor, Prof. Maiken H. Mikkelsen, maiken.mikkelsen@nbi.ku.dk.

jobs.description:
The Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN) invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in computational plant biology. The project is financed by the Novo Nordisk Foundation through the Ascending Investigator grant “Accelerating crop resilience with AI-enabled gene function prediction and stress regulatory networks” (NNF26OC0113093). The programme aims to make heat and drought resilience engineering in Nordic crops predictable by converting the plant literature and multi-omics data into evidence-backed predictions of gene function and stress regulation.

  Start date is expected to be 1 May 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The project  Most plant genes remain functionally uncharacterised, and the knowledge that does exist is scattered across more than 200,000 articles. Our knowledge graph PlantConnectome has shown that large language models can extract this knowledge at scale; this project will build its successor and use it to predict gene function.

  You will:

   	
• Fine-tune open large language models (e.g. Llama-class models with QLoRA) on our existing, curated knowledge graph, and use the best checkpoint to extract entities, relationships and supporting evidence from >200,000 open-access plant articles spanning model species and crops 	
• Build a provenance-aware knowledge graph an order of magnitude larger than PlantConnectome, in which every edge is traceable to the sentence and experiment that supports it 	
• Predict new gene–GO associations by direct-neighbourhood reasoning (matching LLM-generated entity definitions to GO terms with embeddings and an LLM guardrail) and by path-based link prediction with graph neural networks, evaluated CAFA-style against held-out annotations 	
• Turn regulatory relationships in the graph into Boolean and related discrete network models of stress signalling, simulate them, and test their predictions against expression data generated in the group 	
• Distinguish well-supported from over-cited claims, and represent evidence quality and independence explicitly in the graph   The position is computational, but sits in a group that generates its own single-cell stress data and validates predictions in rapeseed, so your predictions will be tested.

  Who are we looking for?  We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of computational biology, bioinformatics, computer science, physics, mathematics or plant biology with a strong quantitative interest. Experience with natural language processing, large language models, graph databases, network modelling or machine learning is an advantage. An interest in how plants actually work is essential; a formal background in plant biology is not.

  What we value  Coding experience is welcome but not required at entry – we teach it. What we cannot teach quickly, and therefore select for, is scientific judgment:

   	
• questioning data rather than accepting it – asking what was measured, how, and against which expectation 	
• noticing anomalies and treating them as information rather than noise 	
• organising several lines of investigation in parallel and knowing when to stop or redirect one 	
• connecting computational evidence to a concrete biological question 	
• changing your mind when the evidence changes   We are equally interested in candidates from biology who want to learn computation and candidates from computer science, physics or engineering who want to learn biology.

  Our group and research – and what do we offer?  The Mutwil group at PLEN works at the interface of comparative and evolutionary plant biology and AI-driven biological discovery. We build large cross-species gene expression atlases, comparative co-expression networks and knowledge graphs, and we use machine learning and large language models to turn the plant literature and omics archives into testable hypotheses. The group comprises several PhD students, postdocs and master’s students, and maintains a portfolio of widely used community resources under the .plant.tools domain, including PlantConnectome, CoNekt, diurnal.plant.tools and evorepro.plant.tools.

Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in generative protein and peptide design for sustainable biomaterials - BRIGHT
jobs.description:
This PhD project is part of a BRIGHT programme developing a general platform for the design of protein- and peptide-based biomaterials, with solid-state battery components as its first testbed. Our goal is to replace fluorinated PFAS polymers with de novo designed proteins and peptides.

You will generate the computational designs at the heart of the platform, by combining molecular foundation models with iterative laboratory feedback. You will develop design algorithms for biomaterials with natural and non-natural amino acids, and for planning their biosynthesis and biomanufacturing. You will develop lab-in-the-loop algorithms that use generative model-controlled stochastic synthesis to maximize information gain at every round of experimental testing.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Responsibilities:

• Generate de novo peptide and protein designs meeting multiple coupled property targets, including adhesion, cohesion, ion conduction and controlled degradability
• Use and adapt generative molecular design tools such as RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN and AlphaFold-type models
• Develop and extend information-dense synthesis algorithms to manufacture designs in the laboratory 
• Extend these methods to expanded genetic codes, so that non-canonical residues can be encoded and biosynthesised rather than only chemically synthesised
• Develop methods to learn from diverse measurements of material properties, via shared latent representations 
• Develop methods to continuously learn from iterative experimentation, by feeding back experimental data into an integrated model with quantified uncertainty
• Work closely with experimentalists to optimize experimental designs for collecting high-information training data
• Work closely with experimentalists to automate and scale up design-build-test-learn cycles
• Report your research results in peer-reviewed scientific publications and international conferences
• Collaborate within the research group and our local, national and international networks
• Disseminate your results through public engagement and social media
• Teach and supervise MSc and BSc students as well as research assistants
Qualifications:

• MSc in computational biology, bioinformatics, biophysics, computer science or a related area
• Programming experience in Python
• Experience with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch
• Excellent English proficiency in written and oral form
• Excellent communication and social skills for working within an interdisciplinary research team
• Strong analytical skills and ability to work independently
Preferred qualifications but not mandatory:

• Knowledge of protein structure and molecular biology
• Experience with protein design tools such as RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN or AlphaFold
• Familiarity with DNA-encoded libraries, genetic code expansion or next-generation sequencing
• Interest in multi-objective optimisation, reinforcement learning, and bridging computational design with experimental realisation
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The starting date is 1 March 2027 (or according to mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position. The period of employment is 3 years.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Carlos Acevedo-Rocha: cargac@dtu.dk

You can read more about BRIGHT at https://bright.dtu.dk/
